6C.3 Children that curse their father or mother are to be put to death.
6C.4 Children that strike their father or mother are to be put to death.
7B.1 If an animal kills a person the animal is to be put to death.

7B.2 If an animal is proven to be aggressive, and its owner has been warned, yet he does not confine it, and it kills a man or woman, then both the animal and the owner are to be put to death. If there is a ransom of money demanded of the owner, it can be paid for the redemption of his life.
7B.3 If an animal shall gore a servant, the owner shall give the servant's master a set amount of money and the animal is to be killed.
7B.5 If one man's animal kills another's animal, then the live animal shall be sold and the money (and the dead animal if it be cattle) shall be divided between them.
7B.6 If an animal which is known to be aggressive kills another animal yet its owner had not confined him, then he shall pay for the animal killed but can keep the dead animal.
7C.4 If a pit is opened or dug and left uncovered, and an animal falls into it, the owner of the pit shall pay the owner of the animal but he can keep the dead animal.
10A.5 If a man acts with premeditation against his neighbor, to kill him with guile, he shall die.
10A.6 One who strikes a man so that he dies is a murderer and shall be put to death.
10C.1 He that kidnaps a man, whether he sells him or he is found in his possession, he shall be put to death.
10E.1 He that strikes his father or mother shall be put to death.
10E.2 He that curses his father or mother shall be put to death.
10I.1 Manslaughter or accidental killing is not punished by death, but the one guilty is to be banished to a city of refuge.
18A.12 You should take appropriate precautions of any dangerous situation on your land which might cause damage or injury to other persons or their property.
19C.1 The restitution and punishment should be according to the crime--Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
19C.4 If one man's animal kills another man's animal, then the live animal is to be sold and the money equally divided between them.
19C.6 Fines are to be assessed by judges for some personal injuries.
19C.9 If two men are quarreling and one injures the other, he shall compensate the injured party for his loss of time and shall provide for him until he is completely healed.

19C.17 If a pregnant woman is inadvertently struck and as a result gives birth prematurely, yet no lasting harm follows, the one who struck her is to be fined as the woman's husband may demand of him and he shall pay as the judges decide. But if any lasting harm follows, then you shall give life for life.
19D.1 Death for murder.
19D.10 Compensation and restitution for lost time, property damage or injury.
21B.6 A maidservant betrothed to her master can be redeemed but cannot be sold to a foreign nation.
21B.7 Those of your race can be in service to you for only six years and are to be freed in the seventh year.
21B.8 If a maid-servant is betrothed to the master's son she shall be treated according to the custom of daughters.
21B.9 A servant, when free from his service, shall be allowed to depart with that which he had when he went into service.
21B.11 If a servant does not want his freedom at the end of six years but desires to remain with his master, he then shall be in servitude to him for life.
21B.16 If a man strikes his servant and he dies at his hand, he shall be punished.
21B.17 If a servant is injured by his master he is then to be set free.
